Set up parallel workers with reproducible random streams

Source: R/core-config.R
wgh_parallel.Rd

A thin wrapper around future::plan(). When a parallel plan is active, the heavy parts of the package run on several workers: bootstrap replicates (quantile regression, quantile mixed models, SITAR intervals, quantile models of child-level outcomes, mediation, phenotype outcome links and cluster stability), the quantile grid of linear quantile mixed models, and the cross-validation folds of the prediction benchmark and the conditional references. Each task gets its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG random stream derived from the function's seed, so the results are identical whether the work runs sequentially or in parallel, and whatever the number of workers.

Usage

wgh_parallel(
  workers = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L),
  strategy = c("multisession", "multicore"),
  max_size = 2
)

Arguments

workers

Number of workers. 1 returns to sequential processing.

strategy

"multisession" (default, separate R sessions, works on all platforms) or "multicore" (forked processes, faster to start but not available on Windows or inside RStudio).

max_size

Largest size of data sent to each worker, in gigabytes. NULL leaves the future.globals.maxSize option unchanged.

Value

The previous plan, invisibly, with the previous future.globals.maxSize value as attribute globals_max_size.

Details

The function also raises the future.globals.maxSize option, because growth data and fitted models often exceed the default limit of 500 MB. The previous value is stored and restored when you return to sequential processing with workers = 1. All arguments are checked before anything is changed, so an invalid call leaves the plan and the option as they were.

Next steps

Check the set-up with wgh_parallel_info(), run any bootstrap or flow as usual, and return to sequential processing with wgh_parallel(1). See vignette("parallel-computing").

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("furrr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  old <- wgh_parallel(2)
  wgh_parallel_info()
  f <- haz ~ splines::ns(age, knots = c(8, 11, 14), Boundary.knots = c(5, 18.5)) * baz
  d <- growdat[growdat$sex == "Female" & growdat$age >= 5, ]
  par <- wgh_rq(d, f, taus = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), anchor_ages = c(9, 12), B = 20)
  wgh_parallel(1)                       # back to sequential, option restored
  seq <- wgh_rq(d, f, taus = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), anchor_ages = c(9, 12), B = 20)
  all.equal(par$slopes, seq$slopes)     # identical results
}
#> Parallel plan: "multisession" with 2 workers.
#> Parallel plan: "sequential" with 1 worker.
#> [1] TRUE
# }
